chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes) during routine health maintenance
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 39-year-old male with a long-standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2011, currently treated with low‑dose lisinopril 10 mg. Blood pressure remains in the stage 1 range (133/79 mmHg). Obesity (BMI ≥30) was documented in late 2018 and persists. Prediabetes has been present since 2002 with a recent HbA1c of 5.9%. Chronic anemia has been noted since 2008, etiology unspecified. He reports ongoing intimate‑partner abuse since 2005 and is employed part‑time since 2018, reflecting socioeconomic stressors. The patient has had predominantly wellness visits, with the last encounter in December 2018, and limited recent engagement with the healthcare system.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple medication review reminders (2016‑2018), gingivitis (2016‑2018), a viral sinusitis episode resolved in 2016, prior full‑time employment resolved in 2018, past stress resolved in 2017, and limited social contact resolved in 2016. These reflect a history of dental issues, occasional acute respiratory infection, and prior changes in employment and psychosocial status.
social_determinants: Part‑time employment suggesting limited income; ongoing intimate‑partner abuse posing safety and mental‑health concerns; higher education indicating health‑literacy potential; resident of Tewksbury, MA; no documented smoking, alcohol, or substance use.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 133/79 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension), heart rate 91 bpm, HbA1c 5.9% (prediabetic). BMI, total cholesterol, LDL, and eGFR are missing, limiting full risk calculation. Comorbidity flags indicate hypertension and anemia. Charlson comorbidity index is 1; clinical complexity is moderate. Elevated risk noted for cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), metabolic (obesity, prediabetes), renal (hypertension without eGFR data), hematologic (anemia), and psychosocial (intimate‑partner abuse, part‑time employment).

clinical_impression: A middle‑aged male with multiple metabolic risk factors (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes) that are suboptimally managed, chronic anemia of unclear etiology, and significant psychosocial stress from intimate‑partner abuse. Limited recent healthcare engagement and several key laboratory data are missing, highlighting gaps that impede comprehensive risk stratification and management.
